summary: Max Leopold Margolis was a scholar in linguistics and religious studies. He studied at Leibniz-Gymnasium Berlin and Columbia University (PhD 1891). He held posts at Columbia, Hebrew Union College, the University of California, Berkeley, and Dropsie College (1909–1932).
Max Lindenau studied at the University of Leipzig under Ernst Windisch, completing his studies by 1913.

Max Oidtmann is a historian, sinologist, and tibetologist. He studied at Carleton College, Indiana University, and Harvard University under Mark Elliott. He held posts at Georgetown University, Georgetown University in Qatar, and became a professor at the University of Munich around 2020.

Max Scheler was a philosopher who studied at the universities of Munich, Berlin, and Jena. He held academic positions at Jena (circa 1901–1906), Munich (circa 1907–1910), Göttingen, and the University of Cologne (circa 1919–1928).
Max Uhle was a scholar of archaeology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Leipzig from around 1876 to 1880 under Georg von der Gabelentz.

Max Walleser worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at Heidelberg, Freiburg, Geneva, and Erlangen-Nürnberg (PhD circa 1902). He served at the University of Heidelberg as Privatdozent (1911) and professor of Indian philology (1918–1936).
Max von Waldberg studied at Chernivtsi University around 1877 to 1881. He later held an academic post at the University of Heidelberg from circa 1889 to 1933.

Maxime Kaltenmark was a scholar of sinology and religious studies. He served as director at the Centre Franco-Chinois d'Études Sinologiques (1946) and École Française d'Extrême-Orient (1949–1953), later holding posts at the EPHE and University of Paris (circa 1957–1979).
May Oung was active in history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Cambridge around 1905 to 1908 and founded the Burma Research Society in 1910.

Maya Jasanoff is a historian who studied at Harvard College, Cambridge, and Yale University. She held a faculty post at the University of Virginia (circa 2003–2009) and became a professor of history at Harvard University around 2009.
McDougal is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts (Research) at the University of Sydney under the supervision of Geoffrey Samuel and Mark Allon.

McKim Marriott was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at Harvard under Clyde Kluckhohn and at the University of Chicago (PhD circa 1955), where he served as professor of anthropology and social sciences from 1955 to 1998.

Medawachchiye Dhammajothi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Sri Jayewardenepura, PGIPBS, and Nanjing University. In 2008, he held posts at the University of Colombo, PGIPBS, and Buddhist and Pali University of Sri Lanka.
Medhani studied under Penor Rinpoche and Dudjom Rinpoche.
Megan Bryson works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology. She studied at Stanford University and was affiliated with the University of Tennessee in 2017.

Megumu Honda was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo and at Yale University under Paul Tedesco and Rulon Wells. He served as professor and professor emeritus at Doho University.
Mei Ching Hsuan is a Tibetologist who earned a PhD at the University of Bonn (attested 2009) under doctoral supervisor Peter Schwieger and teacher Dieter Schuh.

Meiji Yamada is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (attested 1962). He later served as a professor at Ryukoku University, attested from 1963 to 1971 and in 2007.

Meinrad Scheller was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Paris and Zurich under Manu Leumann, Ernst Risch, and Julius Pokorny. He held professorships at Fribourg (1963), Munich (1968–1975), and Zurich (1975).
Meiping Li is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University (attested 2009) under the supervision of Kirill Solonin.
